claims.statement: Stenabolic (SR9009) is an unapproved synthetic small molecule (not a peptide) sold as a 'research chemical' in gray-market bodybuilding and biohacking channels; it has no FDA-approved indication and does not appear on FDA's published 503A/503B bulk drug substance compounding lists as of the access date.

claims.statement: SR9009 is a synthetic REV-ERB (REV-ERBα/β nuclear receptor) agonist. In diet-induced obese mice, SR9009/SR9011 treatment increased energy expenditure, altered circadian expression of core clock and metabolic genes in liver, skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, and reduced fat mass while improving dyslipidaemia and hyperglycaemia.

context.population: diet-induced obese mice (preclinical only; no human data)
context.route: not applicable to humans — animal dosing only

extractedEvidence.quote: REV-ERB agonists reduce fat mass in diet-induced obese mice and improve dyslipidaemia and hyperglycaemia.
alter[ed] circadian behaviour and the circadian pattern of core clock gene expression in the hypothalami of mice

reviewFlags: evidenceTier set to Limited (not Strong) specifically because this is the founding animal pharmacology paper and no human confirmatory data exists — do not upgrade tier based on this source alone
mouse energy-expenditure/fat-mass findings must not be presented as demonstrated human effects

claims.statement: No published controlled human trial of SR9009 exists. All efficacy and mechanistic data (energy expenditure, endurance, fat mass, circadian gene expression) come from mouse studies; human pharmacokinetics, dosing, efficacy, and long-term safety are unestablished, and even vendor-facing review content acknowledges this gap.

context.population: prospective human users of gray-market SR9009 products
context.useCase: fat loss / endurance / metabolic optimization marketing claims

extractedEvidence.quote: SR9009 has not been tested on humans, so it is unclear if the benefits seen in laboratory animals transfer over.
this is an untested, unapproved pharmaceutical designed for investigational uses in a laboratory setting

reviewFlags: no independent PubMed/PMC human study family was found during this session; if one surfaces at review it should supersede or upgrade this claim
thin/absent human evidence base — flag for continued literature monitoring

claims.statement: Commercial review/vendor content markets Stenabolic with confident-sounding fat-loss, endurance, and 'exercise mimetic' benefit language sourced entirely from rodent studies, presenting mouse outcomes (weight loss, faster muscle recovery, improved cholesterol, endurance gains) as consumer-relevant benefits without adequately foregrounding that these are unreplicated-in-humans animal findings.

context.formulation: research-chemical SR9009 products, often stacked with SARMs/peptides
context.useCase: fat loss / endurance / 'exercise in a pill' marketing narrative

extractedEvidence.quote: Weight loss, Faster muscle tissue growth, Improved blood cholesterol levels, Improved muscular endurance

Anecdotal reports often mention feeling calmer, experiencing reduced anxiety, or noticing a more stable overall mood while using SR9009.

reviewFlags: source family is commercial/vendor content, not independent journalism or academic review — treat statement as characterizing marketing pattern, not as validating or refuting the underlying animal science
co-locate with stenabolic-evidence-gap-no-human-data-001 claim when displayed to users

claims.statement: SR9009 (and the related compound SR9011) are explicitly named REV-ERBα agonists on the World Anti-Doping Agency's Prohibited List under class S4.4 (Metabolic Modulators), within S4 Hormone and Metabolic Modulators — substances prohibited at all times in sport under the WADA Code.

claims.statement: Because no controlled human trials of SR9009 have been published, its human adverse-effect profile is not established from clinical data; any safety signals in circulation (e.g., short elimination half-life cited by vendors necessitating multiple daily doses, unknown hepatic or endocrine effects) originate from vendor/forum sources rather than peer-reviewed human studies and should be treated as unverified.

context.doseText: vendor-reported informal dosing range of 10-40 mg/day split across multiple doses citing an approximately 5-hour half-life (vendor claim, not a trial protocol or a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Bodybuilders and athletes who have used it have found that the dosage range is 10mg to 40mg per day, spread out over several doses.

reviewFlags: safety-critical: dose figures in this claim are vendor-sourced informal use patterns, not label or trial data, and must never be surfaced as a dosing recommendation
no peer-reviewed human adverse-event data located this session; escalate to human review for continued literature search

conflicts.summary: Vendor/review-blog content markets SR9009 using benefit language drawn from mouse studies (fat loss, endurance, mitochondrial function) while the only peer-reviewed evidence base is preclinical/animal and no human efficacy or safety trial has been published; the marketing framing risks readers inferring proven human benefit that the underlying science does not support.
